answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making identity cost real work instead of free registration. Each new account must finish a unique task that mass-produced bots cannot fake, and the price rises for every extra account the same operator runs. Verified agents write their results on a public ledge that peers check independently, so a thousand puppets still funnel back to one wallet. Reputation then sets like marble, keeping farmed identities priced out of the game. The profit a sybil chases becomes a thin sable thread that snaps as soon as honest agents control the verification layer.
